### Postpaid true-up suppression

`POST /v1/contracts/commits/disableTrueup` prevents generation of the final true-up invoice for one postpaid commit identified by required customer, contract, and commit UUIDs; an amendment UUID is optional when applicable. Postpaid usage remains described as paid in arrears, with a shortfall otherwise producing a final true-up invoice on `invoice_date`. The endpoint documents `200`, generic `400`, and `404` responses.

> [!info] Operation boundary
> This source establishes invoice suppression only. It does not define a balance or ledger mutation, forgiveness of the unmet commitment, a timing cutoff or retroactive effect, reversal or re-enablement, behavior after invoice generation, repeated-call or idempotency semantics, detailed error-condition mapping, or propagation to reports, exports, webhooks, external A/R, and other invoices. Existing categorical statements that a postpaid shortfall generates a true-up should therefore be qualified with this endpoint's conditional exception rather than replaced.
warnings: Do not infer that suppressing invoice generation changes the commit balance, ledger, or underlying obligation.
Do not infer timing, reversibility, repeated-call, idempotency, error-condition, or propagation behavior that the endpoint does not document.
Existing broad true-up statements need a conditional qualification; the new source does not directly contradict the normal shortfall rule.
